chapter: Eddie South, high school and the South Side scene
title: Taylor's own Eddie South trio and the jazz Rhapsody in Blue arrangement
summary: Taylor tells of writing a swinging Rhapsody in Blue to trip up Eddie South, who sight-played it perfectly.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well in terms of… in one of the things that you said, just for your story, I‟d like to relate to you, many years later I was working with a trio, which was the Eddie South trio and Eddie had thrown all that same material on me.
And, you know, the piano is supposed to sound like a [unintelligible] so you‟re running this piece.
You‟re running all over trying to play all these notes and he‟s playing
So I said doggone it, I‟m young and I‟m just out of school, I said, “I‟m going to fix it‟. As you know it‟s harder to play a different arrangement of something you already played.

I knew he had an arrangement on Rhapsody In Blue so I made this… laboriously sat down and wrote out this very difficult arrangement rhythmically so that we‟re swinging. It‟s not the concert thing, this is a jazz version of Rhapsody In Blue and it had all the same stuff but it‟s swinging. So I said, “I know this is going to hang him”. So I bring it into rehearsal one night… one afternoon and Eddie said, “Aw, that looks nice”, and he picked up his violin and then he played it like he wrote it [laughter].
